steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Audience reception of global film is shaped by cultural context: viewers from different backgrounds interpret the same film differently based on their own values and experiences. | Key Fact: Subtitles preserve the original language performance and cultural authenticity but require active reading and can distract from visual composition. | Key Fact: Dubbing allows viewers to focus entirely on the image but replaces original vocal performances and can flatten cultural specificity through translation choices. | Key Fact: Cultural bridging occurs when a film from one culture resonates with audiences from another, often through universal themes such as family, love or justice.
